title: Reading Drill — Comparing objects found on beaches — Building a comparison
description: One short passage, six questions. Recommended time: 10 minutes.

passages.title: Comparing objects found on beaches — Building a comparison
passages.body:
**A** The beach survey team had been asked to investigate small pieces being counted more often on smoother sections in Ravensmere. Its first task was to decide which signs of improvement could be compared between sites. It settled on objects seen per survey strip, because the same measure could be applied in the original setting and at a second location.

**B** During a eight-week comparison, the team used measuring tapes at both places. It recorded outcomes separately for each site. Because the height of the last tide might influence the figures, the team used a column in the record to show when that condition was present. The surveys included quiet periods as well as busy ones.

**C** The team then put forward a consistent sampling strip. Its report asked for another comparison after the change had been tried. This would distinguish a genuine effect from an improvement that could have occurred anyway. The report did not assume that the more successful site before the change would be the better site afterwards.
